title: Past perfect continuous, past perfect and past continuous

sections.title: Past perfect continuous vs. past perfect
sections.content:
We use the past perfect continuous to talk about something that was in progress recently before or up to a past point in time, and the past perfect when we talk about a finished activity before a past time:
• I'd been doing some work in the garden when Lea arrived, so I didn't hear her come in. (not I'd done some work in the garden when Lea arrived, so I didn't hear her come in.)
• I'd done all the ironing so I started cleaning the windows. (not I'd been doing all the ironing so I started cleaning the windows.)
We can often use either the past perfect continuous or the past perfect with a similar meaning:
• I'd been working / I'd worked hard all year, so I felt that I deserved a holiday.

sections.title: How many times: use past perfect
sections.content:
If we talk about how many times something happened in a period up to a particular past time, we use the past perfect, not the past perfect continuous:
• How many times had you met him before yesterday? (not How many times had you been meeting him?)
• I had stayed in the hotel twice in the 1990s. (not I had been staying in the hotel twice …)

sections.title: Situations going on before a past time
sections.content:
The past perfect continuous can be used to talk about a situation or activity that went on before a particular past time and (i) finished at that time, (ii) continued beyond it, or (iii) finished shortly before it:
• (i) We'd been driving for about an hour when the engine suddenly stopped.
• (ii) She felt terrible during the interview because she had been suffering from flu since the previous day.
• (iii) When I last saw Omar, he'd been running and was out of breath.
If we are not interested in how long the activity went on, we can use the past continuous instead of the past perfect continuous. Compare:
• When the merger was announced it became apparent that the two companies had been discussing the possibility since last year. and
• A friend told me about a conversation she'd recently overheard. Two women were discussing their holiday plans …
• I first met Mateo and Lucia when they had been going out together for five years, and they didn't get married for another three years after that. and
• Karin met Lars when she was going out with his best friend.

sections.title: State verbs: use past perfect only
sections.content:
Remember that we don't describe states with continuous tenses (see Unit 1), and we use the past perfect, not the past perfect continuous, even when we focus on the length of a situation up to a particular past time:
• We had only owned the car for six weeks when the clutch broke. (not We had been owning the car for six weeks …)

sections.title: Past perfect continuous in written texts
sections.content:
The past perfect continuous is mainly used in written texts and is less common in speech. Here is an example in a newspaper article:
• The body of a climber who went missing in the Alps was finally found yesterday. Carl Sims had been climbing alone near the Harz Waterfall, which has claimed many lives in the past.

exercises.question: She ___ only ___ for the company for a couple of months, so I was surprised to hear that she'd left. (apply)
exercises.hint: Use past perfect continuous for an activity in progress before a past event.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had only been working
Use past perfect continuous for an activity in progress before a past event.

exercises.question: She finally ___ her way up from trainee to a management position, and she celebrated her promotion with a big party. (carry)
exercises.hint: For a finished achievement/result, use past perfect simple.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had carried
We use the past perfect here because this action happened before another past event.
💡 For a finished achievement/result, use past perfect simple.

exercises.question: The avalanche ___ them 500 metres down the mountain but no one was hurt. (carry)
exercises.hint: A completed action before a past time uses past perfect simple.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had carried
We use the past perfect here because this action happened before another past event.
💡 A completed action before a past time uses past perfect simple.

exercises.question: She took a bottle from the bag she ___ all the way from home. (carry)
exercises.hint: A completed action (bringing it) before taking it out = past perfect simple.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had carried
We use the past perfect here because this action happened before another past event.
💡 A completed action (bringing it) before taking it out = past perfect simple.

exercises.question: We ___ for visas early, but still hadn't got them by the week before the holiday. (apply)
exercises.hint: Completed action before another past reference.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had applied
We use the past perfect here because this action happened before another past event.
💡 Completed action before another past reference.

exercises.question: She was tired because she ___ (drive) for six hours.
exercises.hint: Extended activity before a past moment explaining its result → past perfect continuous.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had been driving
The past perfect continuous describes an extended activity that occurred before a past moment and explains its result. The tiredness is the present-past result of six hours of driving.

exercises.question: She ___ for jobs, without success, since leaving university.
exercises.hint: Ongoing activity over a period up to a past time = past perfect continuous.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had been applying
We use the past perfect continuous here to show an activity was ongoing before another past event.
💡 Ongoing activity over a period up to a past time = past perfect continuous.

exercises.question: He ___ all the way from New York to be at yesterday's meeting. (fly)
exercises.hint: A completed action before the meeting = past perfect simple.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had flown
A completed action before the meeting = past perfect simple.

exercises.question: When the plane was diverted, shortly after take-off, it ___ from London to Frankfurt.
exercises.hint: An activity in progress at the point of diversion = past perfect continuous.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had been flying
We use the past perfect continuous here to show an activity was ongoing before another past event.
💡 An activity in progress at the point of diversion = past perfect continuous.

exercises.question: Mrs Bishop ___ to have children for years, and only became pregnant at the age of 45.
exercises.hint: Length of an activity up to a past time = past perfect continuous.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had been trying
We use the past perfect continuous here to show an activity was ongoing before another past event.
💡 Length of an activity up to a past time = past perfect continuous.

exercises.question: This was the first time we had been to the castle, even though we ___ Prague a few times before.
exercises.hint: 'How many times' before = past perfect simple.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had visited
We use the past perfect here because this action happened before another past event.
💡 'How many times' before = past perfect simple.

exercises.question: When the rescue team arrived, the climbers ___ (wait) for eight hours.
exercises.hint: Duration of activity before the arrival moment → past perfect continuous.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had been waiting
'For eight hours' signals duration. Since this activity was ongoing before the rescue team arrived, use the past perfect continuous to show both duration and anteriority.

exercises.question: She bought her first watch at the age of eight. It ___ two pounds.
exercises.hint: State verb — use past perfect simple, not continuous.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had cost
We use the past perfect here because this action happened before another past event.
💡 State verb — use past perfect simple, not continuous.

exercises.question: Emma Willems ___ novels for ten years before she published her first book. (write)
exercises.hint: Duration of activity before a past event = past perfect continuous.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had been writing
We use the past perfect continuous here to show an activity was ongoing before another past event.
💡 Duration of activity before a past event = past perfect continuous.

exercises.question: For some time Daniel ___ about passing the exams and eventually decided to change the course he was taking.
exercises.hint: Ongoing mental activity over a period = past perfect continuous.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had been worrying
We use the past perfect continuous here to show an activity was ongoing before another past event.
💡 Ongoing mental activity over a period = past perfect continuous.

exercises.question: My teacher was really annoyed with me. It was the third time I ___ late for school that week.
exercises.hint: 'How many times' (third time) = past perfect simple.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had arrived
We use the past perfect here because this action happened before another past event.
💡 'How many times' (third time) = past perfect simple.

exercises.question: I ___ always ___ it would be easy to get a job, and was disappointed to be rejected.
exercises.hint: State verb 'believe' — use past perfect simple.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had always believed
State verb 'believe' — use past perfect simple. State verbs describe mental states, emotions, or senses and are not normally used in continuous forms.

exercises.question: We ___ about Sarah when, to our amazement, she walked through the door.
exercises.hint: Activity in progress just before a past event = past perfect continuous.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: had been talking
We use the past perfect continuous here to show an activity was ongoing before another past event.
💡 Activity in progress just before a past event = past perfect continuous.
